transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-01
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~53 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Ethan (Redwood SE), Lena (Novum - Procurement), Samir (Novum - Legal), Priya (Novum - SRE), Derek (Novum - Finance)

Summary: (auto) kick-off for vendor gate intake. Focus areas: MSA/DPA redlines, SLA tiers, pricing bands for hosted vs dedicated, KMS/egress, pilot scope and perf validation.

[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for making the time, i'll do a 60 second intro, i'm maya, AE on the redwood inference side. ethan will cover technicals. keen to understand proc/legal blockers and align on next steps.
[00:18] Lena (Novum): thanks maya. quick intro here - lena, head of procurement. samir is with legal, priya handles infra, derek for finance. we have a gate next thursday but can flex if needed. main ask: what are the non-negotiables for redwood and what's realistic on pricing and sla.
[00:35] Maya: perfect, quick agenda: 1) legal redline high level 2) pricing/commits 3) pilot scope & perf 4) KMS/egress/residency 5) next steps. sound ok?
[00:45] Samir (Legal): yep, just to flag — our security team will need SOC 2 + certs and we have a couple DPA asks around subprocessors and data retention. also want clarity on who holds keys, is that customer-managed KMS for private?
[01:05] Ethan (Redwood SE): yeah, good questions. for private we do support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations; for hosted we have bring-your-own-key options with limited tokenization footprint, but some customers keep keys in their KMS and we never persist plaintext.
[01:24] Priya (SRE): when you say limited tokenization, does that mean request bodies are still routed through redwood's control plane? we need to confirm path for sensitive PII — ideally no plaintext leaves our VPC.
[01:38] Ethan: for private deployment we can run in your VPC on customer infra or via our private offering where the control plane is customer-managed. small chance of terminology slip: our 'Redwood Private' is sometimes called 'Redwood Privet' in docs, sorry — but technical guarantee is you can have zero-plaintext egress depending on the deployment profile.
[02:02] Derek (Finance): cost side — can you explain the delta between hosted pricing and dedicated/reserved? we expect burst traffic around holiday spikes and want a predictable monthly bill.
[02:18] Maya: sure. hosted is usage-based (per-token + embeddings units). dedicated gives you reserved capacity at a monthly commit — you pay for the pool and get predictable throughput. there's also a burst pool add-on. main tradeoff: hosted lowers ops lift but can be higher unit cost at scale; dedicated reduces per-token but adds fixed commit.
[02:42] Lena: what about egress charges and data transfer fees? some vendors add per-GB egress on top of per-token.
[02:51] Ethan: we surface egress separately in our pricing. for private deployments within the same cloud region egress is effectively internal; for cross-region or cross-cloud there may be network charges we pass through. We also recommend caching KV prefixes and batching to reduce gross tokens.
[03:18] Samir: legal — MSA question: indemnity and escrow. we typically ask for source escrow triggers. how do you handle code escrow?
[03:28] Maya: most enterprise customers ask for an escrow clause; we have a standard escrow playbook to start. i'll send the MSA redline guidance. quick note: we prefer negotiated language around force majeure and liability caps tied to fees.
[03:44] Derek: and pricing bands for pilot vs production? we don't want surprise overages during pilot.
[03:52] Maya: pilots are usually discounted, we can cap the pilot spend or do a flat fee pilot. we'll provide a pilot price sheet. the ask: we need estimated monthly tokens and peak qps to give an accurate dedicated commit quote.
[04:06] Priya: ok, we can commit ballpark figures by monday. our main constraint is latency — we run user-facing recommendations; latency SLO of <120ms 95th is preferred, but we can accept slightly higher if cost savings are material.
[04:24] Ethan: latency is mainly a function of model size, quantization, and routing/batching. for hosted with smaller models you can hit sub-100ms for short seq. For larger seq or big models 95th can rise. With dedicated you can guarantee tail latency better by pinning capacity and tuning batching windows.
[04:48] Lena: any caveats about tokenization differences? we use different tokenizers in our stack.
[04:55] Ethan: tokens are model-specific; our billing normalizes to token units per model. we'll share a tokenization FAQ and a small script to estimate token counts from sample payloads.
[05:12] Maya: shifting to legal specifics, samir — what are your main MSA blockers?
[05:18] Samir: three items: 1) data residency/transfer 2) liability cap - we typically want higher caps for critical infra 3) audit rights and subprocessors list in the DPA.
[05:30] Maya: understood. we can accept stronger language on residency for private deployments. liability caps are negotiable but often tied to committed spend. audit rights — we provide SOC2 + custom security attestation for higher tiers; for some customers we provide on-site audits under NDA.
[05:50] Samir: good, will flag anything non-negotiable in our internal doc and return redlines.

[06:05] (fast forward technical deep dive)
[06:10] Ethan: quick note on fallback strategies — smart routing can fallback to smaller model variants if a region or pool is saturated, so you avoid user-visible outages. but that implies different output quality and we surfaced that in the release notes.
[06:32] Priya: how are rollouts handled? we need canary and rollback hooks.
[06:38] Ethan: rollouts support canary %, A/B routing, and automatic fallback policies. we also surface per-route tracing in the console and token-level cost breakdowns.
[06:50] Priya: ok that helps ops.

[07:02] Lena: procurement question — we typically require a 60 day termination notice and pro-rated refunds. is that in your standard MSA?
[07:12] Maya: our standard term is 30 days with pro-rata billing; 60 is negotiable for enterprise. i'll note that.
[07:20] Derek: thinking about finance approvals — is there a multi-year discount for a committed dedicated pool?
[07:27] Maya: yes, annual commits get a material discount versus monthly reserved. we can include tiered pricing: 12/24 month commitments with increasing discounts.

[07:40] (transcription artifact: 'KV cash' mentioned)
[07:44] Ethan: also wanted to call out automatic KV cache for repeated prefixes — that can drop token counts significantly for FAQ-style workloads. some docs accidentally call it KV cash in transcripts.

[08:05] Samir: security - what's your position on customer-supplied KMS and HSM? we need to ensure keys never leave our control for certain workloads.
[08:15] Ethan: supported for Private; for Hosted we have a BYOK path using envelope encryption and we can integrate with major KMS providers. HSM direct control is part of our higher-compliance offering.
[08:30] Priya: then for pilot we want to validate end-to-end key handling; can you provide an architecture diagram?
[08:36] Ethan: yes, will attach runbook and diagram.

[09:01] Maya: quick procurement flow question — once legal signs, what's the typical lead time to provisioning a dedicated pool?
[09:09] Ethan: typically 2-4 weeks after contract and payment for reserved pool. Private on-prem deployments can be longer depending on network and firewall configs.
[09:20] Lena: we have an internal procurement gate next Thurs; if we get MSA/DPA comments in 48 hours we can route the redlines.

[09:32] Priya: performance validation — are you willing to do a bench where we run 1k concurrent users and measure 95th latency?
[09:40] Ethan: absolutely. we'd set up a pilot harness and recommend a small synthetic test, plus a sample of real traffic if you can scrub PII.
[09:50] Derek: on billing — can we get burn-rate alerts? we want to avoid a surprise overage during campaign spikes.
[09:58] Maya: yeah console supports alerts and usage thresholds per-route and token. we can also create a custom billing webhook for your finance team.

[10:12] Samir: legal again — subprocessors list. can you provide a current list and commitment to notify on changes?
[10:18] Maya: we maintain a subprocessors list; we commit to a 30 day notice on changes and provide a mechanism for customers to object for material changes.

[10:32] (side note: slight crosstalk)
[10:38] Lena: if we proceed with pilot, what would the SOW look like for tech support and runbook?
[10:44] Ethan: pilot SOW usually includes 4 weeks of run, perf validation, one integration support engineer, and a readout. pricing can be a fixed pilot fee or cap.

[11:00] Maya: ok, let's capture the decisions so far.
[11:05] Maya: Decisions: 1) customer requests BYOK or private for high residency workloads 2) pilot to be flat-fee with perf validation 3) procurement requests MSA redlines by friday 4) security deep-dive to follow.

[11:22] Samir: sounds good. we'll aim to have legal comments by friday.
[11:26] Lena: and procurement will confirm expected spend bands Monday.

[11:34] Priya: one more ops question — what's the rollback path on a model quality regression? we need automatic fallback to previous model version and retain KV cache compatibility.
[11:44] Ethan: there is a rollout feature that pins previous model as fallback; KV cache compatibility is maintained for minor model versions, for major arch changes we'd need to rewarm caches — we'll document the exact constraints in the runbook.

[12:02] Derek: finance — will you provide an estimate of committed cost with a 12 month vs 24 month?
[12:08] Maya: yes, ethan and i will draft a tiered quote and include egress and optional KMS/HSM charges.

[12:20] (closing)
[12:22] Maya: recap and next steps — i'll send the MSA redline summary and the DPA exception table by monday 2026-07-05; ethan will share pilot runbook and perf spreadsheet by 2026-07-07; novum to share token estimates by 2026-07-06; security deep-dive to be scheduled week of 2026-07-13.
[12:45] Lena: thanks everyone. this was useful.
[12:48] Samir: thanks, bye.
[12:50] Maya: thanks, bye.

Notes on transcript quality: occasional mis-hear (KV cash), speaker overlap. References: pilot runbook (link: internal/documents/pilot-runbook-llm.pdf), MSA template (link: internal/legal/MSA-standard-2026.pdf), security pack (link: internal/security/soc2-2025.zip).
